skill_defects: SKILL.md has no upload checklist of its own: unlike the card-format skills ('Upload path — hand over one checklist'), the single-file skill relies only on the shared 'What a manual run actually does, gate by gate' block, so the run must work out from the Gate 3 inputs table (written as '[auto]') that budget, actuals, prior year and driver data are all uploads.

SKILL.md 'Step 4 — Apply materiality filter': 'if not provided, ask — don't assume' and 'If the user declines to set thresholds ... explain everything above zero' leave the unanswered-but-not-declined case open on a run that must proceed.

SKILL.md 'Gate 3' says 'never default ... which budget version is being compared to', but the 'Edge Cases', 'Mid-year budget revision' rule covers only a system holding several budgets; there is no rule for a single uploaded budget with no version name.
SKILL.md 'Step 7 — Roll up and assess full-year impact' assumes a full-year budget exists; no edge case covers a budget supplied for part of the year only.

SKILL.md 'Step 3 — Classify favorable / unfavorable' says to take line type 'from the connected chart of accounts ... rather than inferring it from the account's name'; on the upload path there is no chart of accounts and no stated fallback.
sample_defects: budget_2025.csv is derived from the actuals, not an independent plan: revenue = actual x 1.03 (371,000 x 1.03 = 382,130), COGS = actual x 0.98 (215,180 x 0.98 = 210,876), marketing = 4% of ACTUAL revenue (Sep 18,216 = 4% x 455,400, not 4% x 469,062 = 18,762), bank fees equal actual.

budget_2025.csv includes June professional fees of 16,500, so the expected finding 'one-time 14,000 in June 2025' is not a budget variance (variance 0); expect.findings tests the actuals' history rather than variance against budget.
expect.findings omits the main budget variances: revenue 121,158 (2.9%) U YTD and gross profit 168,576 U YTD, operating income 179,506 U.
Manifest calls the budget 'Approved 2025 budget' but the file carries no version or approval label; the budget covers Jan-Sep only, so no full-year comparison is possible.
Arithmetic of key checks out: Sep marketing 29,146 / 455,400 = 6.4% vs 4.0% norm (+60%); COGS 58.0% Jan-Jun and 60.0% Jul-Sep, so GM 42% -> 40%; June professional fees 16,500 - 2,500 = 14,000.
summary: PASS: rota rejected on content, all 3 findings hit; main variances (revenue -2.9% every month, 115,091 cost-rate) explained with causes left to be confirmed.
